# Press station -- OpenPLC starter

*Generated by `tools/gen_starters.py` from the scene's tag set. Do not edit by
hand; regenerate. The program's logic section is yours.*

**The task.** Run the press in the mode mode.position says (0 MAN, 1 OFF, 2 AUTO), read every scan. AUTO: from Start, stroke the ram down to the bottom-dead-centre switch bdc.no, hold it there for the pot's seconds, bring it back up, and repeat until Stop or the selector leaves AUTO. OFF: the ram goes up and stays up. MAN: the ram goes down only while the two-hand relay's hands.valid is made, and comes back up when it drops or at bdc.no; the next stroke needs both hands off first.

**Done when.** In AUTO the press cycles on its own; turn the selector to OFF mid-stroke and the ram goes straight back up, and does not come down again until AUTO and Start. In MAN a click on both palms together strokes it; click one, wait a second and click the other, and hands.left and hands.right both read true while hands.valid does not -- the ram must not move, because that is what a taped-down button looks like. Take your hands off mid-stroke (a single click holds for two seconds, less than a stroke) and the ram comes back up.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`press_station.st`](press_station.st) | Every I/O point declared at its located address, with an empty logic section. |
| [`mbconfig.cfg`](mbconfig.cfg) | The Slave Device entry that points OpenPLC's Modbus master at the sidecar. |

The walkthrough for OpenPLC itself -- installing, compiling, timing,
troubleshooting -- is [`docs/OPENPLC.md`](../../../docs/OPENPLC.md). This page
is only what is different about this scene.

## Run it

1. Open the scene in FactoryForge: pick "Press station" on the start screen (or launch with --scene=res://templates/press_station.json).
2. **Then** start the sidecar as the Modbus slave. The order matters: the
   addresses below are the ones it hands out for this scene's tags, and a
   sidecar that was already running when you changed scene keeps its old
   addresses and puts the new tags above them.

   In the folder FactoryForge was extracted to:

   ```
   .\factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver modbus-tcp -o port 5502
   ```

   On Linux it is `./factoryforge-sidecar`. If OpenPLC runs in WSL or a VM, add
   `-o host <the address it reaches this machine on>` and read the warning
   it prints. Check the address map it prints against the table below.

   <!-- from-source -->
   (From a source checkout: `python -m factoryforge_sidecar connect ...`
   in `sidecar/`, in place of the command above.)
   <!-- /from-source -->
3. Compile `press_station.st` in OpenPLC (web UI *Programs -> Upload*, or copy it
   into `webserver/st_files/` and run `./scripts/compile_program.sh press_station.st`)
   and copy `mbconfig.cfg` to `webserver/core/`,
   or enter these numbers in *Slave Devices -> Add new device*
   (Generic Modbus TCP device, port 5502, slave id 1):

| Block | Start | Size |
|---|---|---|
| Discrete Inputs (%IX100.0) | 0 | 12 |
| Coils (%QX100.0) | 0 | 7 |
| Input Registers (%IW100) | 0 | 4 |
| Holding Registers - Read (%IW100) | 0 | 0 |
| Holding Registers - Write (%QW100) | 0 | 0 |

4. Start the PLC. To have it marked instead, run the grader in place of the
   3D scene -- same tags, same addresses. Stop the sidecar (Ctrl+C) first,
   then start the grader in one terminal:

   ```
   .\factoryforge-sidecar grade --scene press-station
   ```

   and, in a second terminal, the sidecar with the bus port the grader
   printed:

   ```
   .\factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver modbus-tcp --port <bus port it printed> -o port 5502
   ```

   (`./factoryforge-sidecar` on Linux, in both.)

## I/O

`PLC writes` is an output (a motor, a valve, a lamp); `PLC reads` is an input
(a sensor, a button, a measurement). *Brief* marks the signals the task names;
the rest are there to be used, such as each drive's fault contact. Modbus
addresses are decimal, as the sidecar prints them: `0x10` is coil ten.

| Tag | Direction | Type | Modbus | In the program | Meaning | Brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bdc.nc` | PLC reads | bit | 1x0 | `BdcNc` %IX100.0 | limit switch NC contact: TRUE at rest, FALSE while the lever is pushed | yes |
| `bdc.no` | PLC reads | bit | 1x1 | `BdcNo` %IX100.1 | limit switch NO contact: TRUE while the lever is pushed past its trip point | yes |
| `hands.left` | PLC reads | bit | 1x2 | `HandsLeft` %IX100.2 | left palm button held | yes |
| `hands.right` | PLC reads | bit | 1x3 | `HandsRight` %IX100.3 | right palm button held | yes |
| `hands.valid` | PLC reads | bit | 1x4 | `HandsValid` %IX100.4 | the two-hand relay's permissive: both held AND pressed within 0.5 s -- not left AND right | yes |
| `mode.position` | PLC reads | int | 3x0 + 3x1 | `ModePositionHi` %IW100 + `ModePositionLo` %IW101 -> `ModePosition` : DINT | selector position, 0-based, in the order MAN,OFF,AUTO; it stays where it is put | yes |
| `panel.estop` | PLC reads | bit | 1x5 | `PanelEstop` %IX100.5 | E-stop, normally closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = pressed; stays pressed until pulled out | yes |
| `panel.green` | PLC writes | bit | 0x0 | `PanelGreen` %QX100.0 | green lamp on the panel |  |
| `panel.red` | PLC writes | bit | 0x1 | `PanelRed` %QX100.1 | red lamp on the panel |  |
| `panel.reset` | PLC reads | bit | 1x6 | `PanelReset` %IX100.6 | Reset button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `panel.setpoint` | PLC reads | float | 3x2 + 3x3 | `PanelSetpointHi` %IW102 + `PanelSetpointLo` %IW103 -> `PanelSetpoint` : REAL | the operator's pot, 0.5..5 s (starts at 1) | yes |
| `panel.start` | PLC reads | bit | 1x7 | `PanelStart` %IX100.7 | Start button, momentary: a short pulse per press -- latch it | yes |
| `panel.stop` | PLC reads | bit | 1x8 | `PanelStop` %IX101.0 | Stop button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `ram.extend` | PLC writes | bit | 0x2 | `RamExtend` %QX100.2 | extend coil (5/2 valve, no spring: the rod stays where it was last driven) | yes |
| `ram.extended` | PLC reads | bit | 1x9 | `RamExtended` %IX101.1 | reed switch at full stroke | yes |
| `ram.fault` | PLC reads | bit | 1x10 | `RamFault` %IX101.2 | TRUE = the cylinder has seized |  |
| `ram.retract` | PLC writes | bit | 0x3 | `RamRetract` %QX100.3 | retract coil | yes |
| `ram.retracted` | PLC reads | bit | 1x11 | `RamRetracted` %IX101.3 | reed switch at home; mid-stroke neither reed is made | yes |
| `tower.green` | PLC writes | bit | 0x4 | `TowerGreen` %QX100.4 | tower lamp, green | yes |
| `tower.red` | PLC writes | bit | 0x5 | `TowerRed` %QX100.5 | tower lamp, red | yes |
| `tower.yellow` | PLC writes | bit | 0x6 | `TowerYellow` %QX100.6 | tower lamp, yellow | yes |

## Three things this scene's wiring does not forgive

- **A 32-bit value is two registers**, high word first. This scene has 2:
  `mode.position`, `panel.setpoint`. The program's first and last sections
  move them between the registers and plain DINT/REAL variables, so your logic
  never sees a register. OpenPLC's `DWORD_TO_REAL` converts the *number*
  (`16#3F800000` becomes 1065353216.0, not 1.0), so the starter rebuilds a
  REAL bit by bit instead. [`../check_starters.sh`](../check_starters.sh)
  compiles the helpers with OpenPLC's own matiec and checks them against two
  million bit patterns.
- **Anything polled can be missed if it is short.** OpenPLC's master reads
  every 50 ms. A button click in the 3D scene holds its tag for 0.2 s (the
  panel's Press Hold setting) and then leaves it off for at least as long, so
  every click is read several times: act on its rising edge, not its level.
  The grader holds each press for 0.15 s. The same goes the other way: hold an
  output you want the scene to see for well over one polling period.
- **An output you never write is FALSE.** The master rewrites the whole coil
  block on every poll, including coils your program does not touch.
